tips.title: Aligning Wing Parts with a Meng Jig
tips.text: For multi-part wings like Meng's Bf 109E, use their dedicated jig to ensure perfect alignment. Attach the jig to your work surface. Place the wing parts in the jig, matching the locating pins. Glue the parts together using Tamiya Extra Thin Cement, applying it sparingly along the edges. Allow curing for 30 minutes, then remove the wing assembly from the jig.

tips.title: Installing Eduard Photo-Etch Parts
tips.text: For Eduard photo-etch parts, use tweezers and gently bend the parts over a sharp edge to ease them into the desired shape. Apply a small amount of super glue (CA glue) to the back of the part, then carefully position it onto the model. Allow the glue to set for a few seconds before letting go. If a part is too small, use a GodHand nipper to snip it in half, then glue each piece individually.

tips.title: Strengthening Thin Parts with Brass Rod
tips.text: Strengthen thin parts from kits like ICM's T-34 with brass rod. Cut the rod to length with a sharp knife or nippers. Apply CA glue to one end of the rod, then insert it into a drilled hole in the part. Hold the part in place for a few seconds until the glue sets. Once set, trim any excess rod with nippers.

tips.title: Assembling Multi-Part Gun Barrels (Trumpeter)
tips.text: Kits like Trumpeter's Tiger I have multi-part barrels. Dry-fit the parts first, applying a touch of CA glue where they join. Allow curing, then gently pull the parts apart. Glue the parts together using Vallejo Acrylic Thinner as a solvent, applying it along the seam. Once cured, sand the seam with 400 grit sanding sticks, then polish with micromesh cloth.

tips.title: Handling Resin Conversion Kits (Arma Hobby)
tips.text: Resin conversion kits like Arma Hobby's Pz.Kpfw. IV Ausf. G can be delicate. Before gluing, gently clean any mold lines with a needle file. Glue the conversion parts to the kit using super glue, applying it sparingly along the edges. Allow curing for a few minutes before handling. For any gaps, use Vallejo Plastic Putty, letting it dry before sanding.
